National Insurance Company Limited vs Lanka Ranuka Devi 2
Ors on 21 March, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A. No.3816 of 2012
Judgement:
The appellant is the third respondent in M.V.O.P.No.101 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge (Ftc), Bhimavaram and the respondents are the
petitioner and respondents 1 and 2 in the said case.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.

sentences.text:
3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under sections 166 and 163(A) of Motor Vehicles Act against
the respondents by praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- towards
compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on
16.12.2006.

4. The case of the claimant is that on 13.12.2006 the petitioner along with her husband went to
Hyderabad on business purpose in Mini lorry bearing No.AP 16 X 2599 and after attending their
business work, on 16.12.2006 at about 8.30 p.m. the petitioner Vgkrj Macma 3816 of 2012 along
with her husband started from Hyderabad in the same Mini lorry and when reached near
Nandigama at a distance of 5 Km, the first respondent being driver of mini lorry, drove the vehicle
in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the stationed tractor and truck, resulting which
the petitioner and her husband sustained multiple injuries and the petitioner claimed an amount of
Rs.5,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by her.
5. The first and second respondents remained exparte.

The third respondent filed counter by
denying the claim application and contended that the claimant is not entitled any compensation and
the third respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the petitioner injured sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident on
16.12.2006 at about 8.30 p.m. due to rash and negligent driving of the mini lorry
bearing No.AP 16X 2599, driver by its 1st respondent?

ii. Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim the
compensation, if so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?
iii.
To what relief?
7. On behalf of the petitioner, Pw1 to Pw4 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A15 were marked.

On
behalf of respondent No.3, Rw1 was examined, but no document was marked.

8. After considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was
occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an
amount of Rs.3,27,467/- to the claimant towards compensation.
9. Aggrieved by the same, the third respondent/ Insurance company filed the present appeal.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
 Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any
 interference?

Vgkrj Macma 3816 of 2012
11. Point:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 13.12.2006 the petitioner along with her husband went to
Hyderabad on business purpose in a Mini lorry bearing No.AP 16 X 2599 and after attending their
business work, on 16.12.2006 at about 8.30 p.m. the petitioner along with her husband started from
Hyderabad in the same Mini lorry and when reached near Nandigama at a distance of 5 Km, the
first respondent being driver of mini lorry, drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and
dashed against the stationed tractor and truck, resulting which the petitioner and her husband
sustained multiple injuries and the petitioner got treatment in different hospitals.

The injuries
sustained by the petitioner are severe injuries and due to the accident, the injured lost an eye and
her face was disfigured and the injured spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards the medical and
other expenditure and she was in hospital for more than 10 days and she used to get treatment form
her house also.
First and second respondents were set exparte.

Third respondent filed counter by
pleading that the petitioner is an unauthorized passenger in the mini lorry and that the Insurance
company is not liable to pay any compensation.

Vgkrj Macma 3816 of 2012
12.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner herself got examined as Pw1 and got
exhibited Ex.A1 to Ex.A15.

The evidence of Pw1 coupled with Ex.A1 attested copy of First

Information Report, Ex.A3 attested copy of charge sheet clearly goes to show that due to rash and
negligent driving of driver of the mini lorry only the accident was occurred and the claimant, who is
travelling in the said mini lorry, fell down and sustained severe injuries.

sentences.text:
Therefore, in view of the
above reasons
, because of the rash and negligent driving of driv
er of mini lorry only, the accident was occurred.

13. In order to prove the claim of the petitioner, due to the accident, she sustained grievous injuries and lost an eye and her face also disfigured, the petitioner got examined PW2/Dr.V.Lakshmi Prasanna, who treated the petitioner in Andhra Hospital, Vijayawada.

As per the evidence of PW2,
she treated the petitioner in Andhra Hospital, Vijayawada from 17.12.2006 to 28.12.2006 and issued Ex.A2 wound certificate opining that the injuries are grievous in nature, for which the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards the said two grievous injuries (Rs.25,000/- for VGKRJ MACMA 3816 of 2012 each grievous injury) sustained by her.
As per the medical bills submitted by the petitioner, she incurred an amount of Rs.1,62,467/- towards her treatment.
So, the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.1,62,467/- towards compensation.
As per the evidence of PW4-Dr.Mehaboob, he conducted operation to the injuries of PW1 and the petitioner has to rehabitated with dentures in future and it approximate cost is Rs.20,000/-.

Hence, the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenditure and Rs.35,000/-
towards pain, suffering and mental agony and the learned Tribunal also granted an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards disability sustained by her.
The learned Tribunal also granted an amount of Rs.35,000/- towards loss of earnings by giving cogent reasons.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.
In total, the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,27,467/- to the petitioner towards compensation.
In the appeal grounds filed by appellant, the quantum is not disputed.
The contention of appellant is that Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation, because the petitioner is gratuitous passenger.
There is no need to VGKRJ MACMA 3816 of 2012 interfere with the said quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

14. It is the contention of the learned counsel for Insurance Company that the petitioner was travelling in the offending vehicle as an unauthorized passenger, hence, the third respondent/
Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

As per the material available on record,
the crime vehicle/Mini lorry was insured with Insurance Company under Ex.B1 copy of policy and the driver of mini lorry also possessed valid driving licence to drive the mini lorry.

Therefore, since the driver of mini lorry is having valid and effective driving licence by the date of accident and the crime vehicle is insured with 3rd respondent Insurance Company and the policy is also on force and in view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India (three Judge Bench) of Singh ram Vs.,
Nirmala and others1, the Insurance Company shall pay the claim at first instance and later recover the same from the owner of the crime vehicle.

sentences.text:
In the judgment of Manuara Khatun and others Vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh and others2 it was held that the direction to United India Insurance Company Limited being the insurer of the offending vehicle which was found involved in causing accident due to negligence of its driver needs to be issued directing them (United India Insurance Company Limited/ respondent No.3) to first pay the awarded sum to the appellants (claimants) and then to recover the paid awarded sum from the owner of the offending vehicle without filing any independent suit by filing an Execution Petition against the owner of the crime vehicle.
16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the 3rd respondent/ Insurance company is directed to pay the total claim of Rs.3,27,467/- to the claimant at first instance, later recover the same from respondent No.2 by filing Execution Petition without filing independent suit, since the second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
17.

In the result, this appeal is disposed of, by modifying the order dated 26.04.2012 passed in M.V.O.P.No.101 of 2010 on the file of (2017) 4 Supreme Court Cases 796 VGKRJ MACMA 3816 of 2012 the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge (FTC), Bhimavaram.

sentences.text:
It is held that the claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,27,467/- with interest @7.5%
p.a., from the date of petition, till the date of payment.

The 3rd respondent/ Insurance Company is directed to pay the claim amount, within one month from the date of this judgment, to the claimant at first instance and later recover the same from respondent No.2 by filing an Execution Petition and without filing any independent suit.
On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the same along with costs and accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO,J Dated: 21.03.2023.
